method: Eight varying inputs, parity checked. Instant, PlainTime, ISO dates, PlainDateTime arithmetic/rounding, zoned cases and Duration including month prefixes with plain/zoned relative anchors; all16 calendars and owned IANA data included. 1000 warmup +five samples x5000 calls, except transitions128 warmup +five x512. Reference temporal-polyfill1.0.7 basic uses FormatJS native DateTimeFormat with registered native en locale/number pack and owned IANA data on Hermes. Locale/timezone registration excluded from hot timings. Separate TS/Rust and source/HBC processes. Final benchmarks serialized after tests; partial native namespace, one host. PlainDateTime differences span one month, three days, two hours and481 nanoseconds. Added date-time operations include result formatting. Zoned hour rounding uses halfEven; civil-day queries measure startOfDay and hoursInDay. Zoned add/difference now use high-level Rust operations. Four added plain parser workloads read Date.day, DateTime.nanosecond, YearMonth.month and MonthDay.day; every workload uses eight distinct strings. Existing zoned parse includes grammar and resolution. All16 calendar packs remain included; ISO throughput only.

result.scope: Public Instant/PlainTime/ISO-date/PlainDateTime/zoned/Duration workloads; Rust ISO/Instant/PlainTime/calendar/timezone/Duration/plain/zoned arithmetic and string parser JSON bridge optional, all16 calendars and IANA records bundled, date formatting and remaining short-date arithmetic TS. Reference temporal-polyfill 1.0.7 basic implementation. timeParse/timeAdd read nanosecond; timeRoundFormat includes formatting. Zoned cases include gaps/folds/half-hour and skipped-day changes. Transition cases use512 iterations and128 warmup. Not complete native Temporal or WASM comparison.
result.intlProvider: FormatJS native DateTimeFormat with registered en locale and owned IANA data
